newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property stocks rocked by real estate concerns.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks rocked by real estate concerns.

text.p: Expectations of imminent government moves to curb rising real estate prices in Hong Kong rocked share prices of the territory's major property developers once again on Wednesday, dragging down the rest of the market.
The properties sub-index was down 367 points, or 1.54 percent, by late morning at 23,441 points. The Hang Seng blue chip index tumbled 211 points, or 1.48 percent, to 14,095.

"Lots of rumours are flying around as to what is likely to be introduced and the more severe the announcement, the more it will affect the property market and property stocks," said Martin Tacon, senior associate at CS First Boston.
Hong Kong's incoming government is widely expected to impose measures soon after the territory reverts to China on July 1.
Measures to increase supply would ultimately be positive for the property market and developers, analysts said.
"Longer term, with new property measures, the market will be healthier," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

But property developer stocks would be hurt if demand side measures were introduced, said Tacon. "They will reduce the numbers of buyers in the market and by definition, demand side would be short term and not address the real problem," he said.
Shares Cheung Kong fell HK$1.75 to HK$72.25, Sun Hung Kai Properties tumbled HK$1.25 to HK$85.75 and Hysan Development was off HK$0.50 at HK$22.60.
New World Development shed HK$0.40 to HK$44.30 and Hang Lung Development fell HK$0.30 to HK$14.05.
